boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen New Hope Church record (May 25-26, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. The Etowah crossing (May 23) and Wheeler's raid on Cassville (May 24) are context before the frozen dates; Pickett's Mill (GA012, May 27) and Dallas (GA011, May 26-June 1) are separate records that overlap the same lines. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name the two armies without counts; the live field reads zero. Cox says Hooker's three divisions assaulted in columns of brigades, first against a Confederate advance guard of two Alabama regiments and Austin's Sharpshooters that made Geary think he faced a larger force. Johnston says Stewart's division was attacked by Hooker's corps and that more Confederate infantry and artillery were engaged on the 25th than on the 27th. Cox's Appendix A says Quarles's brigade joined near New Hope Church with 2,200 effectives.
claims.rationale: Formations and one brigade figure; no matched count of troops engaged is inspected and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Cox describes a wooded valley in front of New Hope Church with open fields to the north, a Confederate line on wooded ridges with open valleys before it, an assault through dense wood, and a thunderstorm during the fight. Johnston says his troops were not entrenched in either the New Hope Church or the May 27 action. Cox disputes this, saying Johnston's statement rests on his subordinates' reports and that Hooker's division commanders drove the Confederate advance within entrenched lines.
claims.rationale: Ground from an interested history and report, with a direct dispute over entrenchment; no map verification. The Confederate position was taken on the 25th and is not tagged inherited.

claims.rationale: Attributed knowledge from interested accounts and a summary; no message log inspected.

claims.value: Cox says Hooker's columns assaulted Hood's position again and again, and that at the Etowah crossing on the 23rd Hooker took Schofield's pontoons and Schofield lost the afternoon waiting, which Cox calls characteristic of Hooker. Johnston says Stewart's division repulsed Hooker's corps after two hours. The frozen commanders are General Joseph E. Johnston, Major General William T. Sherman and Major General Joseph Hooker; the live page gives General William Sherman and Lieutenant Colonel Joseph Johnston.
claims.rationale: Attributed judgments from an interested history (Cox's own corps was delayed by Hooker) and report; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and the live ranks are not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Total unknown (US 1,600; CS unknown); the live field reads 1015 (US 665; CS 350). Johnston puts his own loss in each of the May 25 and 27 actions at about 450 killed and wounded, estimates the Union loss on the 27th at 3,000 at least, and says it was probably greater on the 25th. Cox gives only a May total for the whole army (context).
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Johnston's 3,000 is an estimate derived from a count of dead on the 27th; it is not a New Hope Church return. Cox's monthly total is not assigned here.

open_questions: Hooker's, Geary's, Williams's and Butterfield's reports, Hood's and Stewart's reports on May 25, the compiled returns and Wheeler's Cassville report remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Johnston's October 20, 1864 report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, is a third family (interested Confederate account). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
